pages.page_title: Franciszek Sterczewski i Klaudia Jachira przeciw Berkowi w TK. Wyłom w KO - Wydarzenia w INTERIA.PL
pages.capture_answer: The KO member who did not back Maciej Berek is Franciszek Sterczewski, KO MP from Poznań. The body places him among KO non-voters; only Klaudia Jachira (KO) voted against, though the headline lists both as 'przeciw'. The quarrel: after the Sejm vote, fellow KO MP Bartosz Arłukowicz posted 'To jest wojna. I to nie czas na dylematy' and attacked him; Sterczewski replied 'Albo bronimy zasad, albo niczym się nie różnimy od tych, którzy je łamią'. Arłukowicz also wrote about 'Święczkowskiego' and needing 'twardych zawodników'. The Sejm then elected Berek with 226 votes in favour. Date: not in the returned text.

followup_urls.why: Related article on the Sejm vote on Berek; may give the vote date.

pages.page_title: Konkurs grantowy Funduszu Obywatelskiego finansowany ze środków norweskiej Nagrody Rafto pod Honorowym Patronatem RPO | Rzecznik Praw Obywatelskich
pages.capture_answer: Civic Fund (Fundusz Obywatelski) grant competition funded by the financial part of the 2018 Rafto Prize, awarded to RPO Adam Bodnar and the Biuro RPO; the Norwegian Rafto Foundation passed it to the Fund at the laureates' wish. All of it goes through this competition, in two areas: judicial independence in Poland, and rights of women and/or sexual minorities and/or migrants. Dates: page header 2018-12-21 and 2019-01-31; publication 2019-01-09; launch planned for early January 2019; applications until 31 January 2019 at 14:00; projects run to end of 2019. Budget: no sum given. Evaluation panel: none named. Honorary patronage: RPO. Results item (R003) dated 2019-03-01 in the 'Zobacz także' list.

pages.publisher: Ministerstwo Sprawiedliwości (Ministry of Justice), Sejm attachment
pages.capture_answer: A 27 June 2025 Ministry of Justice reply, signed by Podsekretarz Stanu Maria Ejchart, to Sejm question no. 2453 by Dariusza Mateckiego on NGO financing from units under the Ministry. It says those units do not fund NGOs, NGO money came from agreements under the previous ministry leadership, and Adam Bodnar was minister when the Justice Fund rules changed (regulation of 13 Nov 2024). It names no grant recipient, organisation or amount in the returned text; the grant list is said to be attached but is absent. Attachments i07583, i10776, i09828 and i10436 were not supplied or fetched.

He presents Maciej Berek as a candidate for TK judge and lists Berek's career: Senate Chancellery legislative office, NIK legal office, eight years as president of the Government Legislation Centre, and academic posts in Lublin and Warsaw. pages.publisher: Sąd Arbitrażowy przy Krajowej Izbie Gospodarczej w Warszawie (SA KIG)
pages.capture_answer: The SA KIG news item (published 13 March 2025) says a Presidium resolution of the Polish Chamber of Commerce dated 13 March 2025 appointed Prof. Marcin Dziurda as a member of the Arbitration Council for the term 2023-2026. The appointment came from PCC president Marek Kłoczko. No vice-president role or date for Dziurda appears on the page. Other roles listed: professor at the Chair of Civil Procedure, Faculty of Law and Administration, University of Warsaw; member of the Civil Law Codification Committee; President of the State Treasury Solicitor's Office 2006-2012.

pages.capture_request: Who authored the HFHR opinion on the TK bill.
pages.fetch_note: Fetched as given: application/pdf, 65,347 characters; returned as text, no file saved. Text came back in two parts, both verbatim: characters 0 to 39,382, then from 39,382 to the end (footnote 41 and the closing funding line). Title and date on the first page: 'Opinia Helsińskiej Fundacji Praw Człowieka do projektu ustawy o Trybunale Konstytucyjnym (Sejm X kadencji, druk sejmowy nr 253)' and 'Warszawa, 30 kwietnia 2024 r.' An earlier cut-off return said neither appears; the verbatim text shows both. The page calls the author 'Helsińska Fundacja Praw Człowieka' (HFPC); the URL domain is hfhr.pl. No individual author, signatory, reviewer or contributor is named, and there is no signature block. No judge, minister, President or Prime Minister is named. Names appear only in footnotes as authors of cited works, not contributors: T. Grzegorczyk, K. Weitz, P. Tuleja, M. Florczak-Wątor, P. Czarny, B. Naleziński, P. Radziewicz, P. Wiliński, P. Karlik, L. Bosek, M. Safjan, L. Bosek M. Wild, B. Banaszak, P. Ochmann, M. Szwed, M.Szuleka, M. Wolny, P. Brzuszczak, K. Ferenc, A. Bodnar, B. Grabowska, P. Osik. Wirtualna Polska (footnote 19) and ECHR judgments appear only as cited sources. The opinion says the transitional provisions were covered in a separate opinion ('odrębnej opinii'), which is not linked.
pages.page_title: Opinia Helsińskiej Fundacji Praw Człowieka do projektu ustawy o Trybunale Konstytucyjnym (Sejm X kadencji, druk sejmowy nr 253)
pages.capture_answer: The opinion (Warsaw, 30 April 2024; Sejm X term, druk 253) is issued by the Helsinki Foundation for Human Rights, which the page calls 'Helsińska Fundacja Praw Człowieka' (HFPC). No individual author or signatory is named, so the foundation itself is the author. The opinion states that the bill was prepared by the Legal Experts Team of the Stefan Batory Foundation and then filed by a group of ruling-coalition MPs (unnamed). Its closing line says the opinion was prepared within HFPC activities co-financed from the Norwegian Funds under the Program Aktywni Obywatele – Fundusz Krajowy. Footnote 13 lists 'A. Bodnar' as co-author of a cited 2010 chapter; that is a citation, not authorship of this opinion.

pages.page_title: Judicial Watch Sues State Dept for Records on Grants to Left-Wing European NGOs
pages.capture_answer: Only second-hand; it is not a grant list. The release (March 09, 2026) cites two ties: that the Free Courts Foundation received a $130,000 grant from the Open Society Foundations in 2023, according to the OSF website, and that Free Courts lists the National Endowment for Democracy as a 'partner organization' on its website. It gives no NED amount, date or fellowship, and calls NED 'quasi-governmental'. No US government contract, grant or payment to Free Courts or to Michał Wawrykiewicz is stated. The only US-government funding item is a project of Ökotárs Alapítvány (Hungarian Environmental Partnership Foundation) supported by the U.S. Embassy Budapest’s Free Media Grant Program. Wawrykiewicz is described only as a 'Polish lawyer' who co-founded Free Courts and sits on the board of DemoCrisis; no MEP role or party is stated. The page uses 'Free Courts (Wolne Sądy)' and 'Free Courts Foundation'; it does not use 'Fundacja'.

pages.page_title: Lawyers from ‘Free Courts’ win European Citizens' Prize
pages.capture_answer: The 2021 WBJ article reports that lawyers 'on the initiative of' Free Courts were awarded the European Citizens' Prize of the European Parliament. The European Parliament is the prize's organiser; the article names no sponsor, no prize money, no award year (only the article date) and no individual awardee. The page says the prize has been awarded since 2008 and can go to individuals or initiatives from all EU Member States. Free Courts is called an 'informal initiative', founded in 2017, 'represented by' Maria Ejchart-Dubois, Sylwia Gregorczyk-Abram, Paulina Kieszkowska-Knapik and Michał Wawrykiewicz. The article gives no titles, party or MEP status for Wawrykiewicz, and does not describe the four as co-founders or awardees. On the lead question, it names no US government money, no National Endowment for Democracy and no fellowship. The article credits EURACTIV.pl as its source and the photo to 'Free Courts (via Facebook)'. The match to the WJP page's 'Free Courts Foundation' rests on the name and the 2017 founding year only.

pages.page_title: Controversial Poland NGO Funding Bill Becomes Law
pages.capture_answer: Context on Polish NGO funding rules. This LibertiesEU article, dated October 16, 2017, reports that Poland's president signed a bill on NGO funding and that the law creates the National Freedom Institute, which will control distribution of public funds from the government and the EU among Poland's 100,000 NGOs. International human rights organisations and a coalition of domestic NGOs had asked President Andrzej Duda (the page states no party for him) to veto it. The article says the bill 'may be used to undercut groups with missions that conflict with the ruling party's positions'. It names none of the listed organisations, no EU programme beyond the general reference to EU public funds, no US funder, and no 2024-26 payment, so it cannot answer the lead question. The page links no 2024-26 source.

pages.page_title: Trump team overrides Congress in last-minute foreign aid push
pages.capture_answer: No Polish or EU tie, and the article does not support the Biden-era speculation. It covers the outgoing Trump administration in January 2021, before Biden took office (it refers to 'President-elect Joe Biden’s incoming administration'). USAID sent an unusually large number of congressional notifications, the State Department 'blown' six congressional holds (five of which pertain to USAID), and the funding in the notifications 'ballooned' to roughly $5 billion since the 2021 fiscal year began in October. An anonymous source gives one motive as 'to tie the hands of the incoming administration'. That is Biden's incoming administration, acted on by the outgoing team, so it does not describe Biden-era spending. The only precedent it cites is 'former President Barack Obama’s administration also ramped up spending before leaving office'. It does not mention Poland, the EU, CERV, AgoraEU, EEA or Norway grants, EU prizes, or any listed NGO.

It answers 67 parliamentary queries from MP Dariusz Matecki, about 86 civil-law contracts (with annexes) the ministry concluded in 2024, as one collective reply. The reply argues that the queries do not meet the rules for parliamentary queries and asks that this collective reply be accepted in place of separate replies. Footnote 1 cites related case numbers BK-VII.0520.87.2026 to BK-VII.0520.155.2026 without links.

The 8 March 2012 e-prawnik.pl article reports the Tribunal's ruling in case K 3/10 on the February 2009 amendment to the Act on Legal Advisers. Per the article, the Tribunal found constitutional the rule that lets persons holding judge or prosecutor posts, and persons practising as advocates or notaries, enter the profession without the legal-adviser exam. The article names no TK judge (not Taborowski) and mentions neither registers nor the TK Act's other-activity rules. It also reports that the Ministry of Justice (resort sprawiedliwości) was preparing simpler access rules, with a proposal to cut the required practice to three years; no minister is named.

The document is a Constitutional Tribunal resolution (uchwała W. 2/92 of 25 March 1992, Dz.U. 1992 Nr 36 poz. 159), not the Constitutional Tribunal Act. Each page carries the stamp '©Kancelaria Sejmu s. N/10 99-08-04'. Line breaks in quoted excerpts are collapsed to single spaces.
pages.page_title: UCHWAŁA TRYBUNAŁU KONSTYTUCYJNEGO z dnia 25 marca 1992 r. (W. 2/92)
pages.capture_answer: The lead question is not resolved. This PDF is not the Constitutional Tribunal Act. It is the Tribunal's resolution of 25 March 1992 (W. 2/92; Dz.U. 1992 Nr 36 poz. 159) on arts 23(1), 26 and 28(1)(2) of the Act on Legal Advisers of 6 July 1982. Its holding: entry on the legal advisers' list of a person practising as a judge or prosecutor is inadmissible. Remigiusz Orzechowski's separate opinion (6 April 1992) disagrees, and reads art. 26 as banning only simultaneous practice. Maciej Taborowski and the other 2026 actors are not named. The resolution cites the Constitutional Tribunal Act of 29 April 1985 only as its procedural basis and reproduces none of its text, so the TK Act's other-activity rules are not answered here. The TK Act itself would need to be located and read; no link to it is on this page.
